quote: I would come back on another evening, on the laptop. I would do that only if the first hours had decisions in them and my saved place were kept. I would not leave it running.

I might come back another evening, on desktop only, if I could answer Dai (Morgan's question, who the town people are) and each step cost far less than half a minute of waiting. I would not leave it running.
Maybe, on another evening and only on desktop, and only if each night asked me for more than about four choices; I would not leave it running.

No. I would close it and not come back on my own, on either device, and I would not leave it running. I might come back only if someone first explained, in plain words, what "dark corners" and "arrangements" are, and showed me one job to do.
Not by choice for twelve nights of this. I would come back once if I could see the town and the river, and if each night gave me a new kind of clue instead of the same misread at the same hour.
Cut or shorten the repeated "optional chapter" paragraph. It appears twice in the log and once more above the gauges. I read it as paperwork.
On the phone, show the level and gauges above the italic note. Stop the recording banner covering them.

Explain a job in one plain sentence. For example: "Pick how many turns to open the gate. More turns lower the water." Drop "How Dai expects to feel", "insist" and the "caught" rule from that first view.
Give me more to decide each night. I made about 3 to 5 choices in 3.5 to 6.5 minutes and spent the rest waiting.
Let me answer Dai, or ask him about himself and the town.
After I set the gate, show what it is doing to the level without making me ask Dai again. I did not see where the 3.6 m reading would lead.

Pause the clock while I read an inspection panel. It says "Time continues slowly while this inspection is open", and 16 game minutes (22:36 to 22:52) still went by on desktop while I read the gate panel.

at 00:11 Dai said "I read four point three. It looks fine." The level gauge still read "4.30 m, read 23:25". The line below it said "was 4.3, read 23:25". I could not tell whether the gauge failed to update or the 00:11 report was not applied. I am guessing.
Show the town and the river, or at least a bridge gauge, during play. The title chart has a bridge line, but I never saw one once the game started.
Make nights differ in shape, not only in their numbers. On both devices the lightning came at 22:34 and a wrong high reading arrived soon after.
Watch arrangements has no Save button, and "Leave this request" is ambiguous.
On the desktop my first level request vanished without an answer (35 s).
